info.title: Nasiko Control Plane API
info.description: A2A orchestration control plane: agent lifecycle, routing, observability, and secrets.

get.summary:
List agents visible to the caller (superuser → all; otherwise owner ∪
public ∪ user-grant — see `agent_access_predicate`).

post.summary: Register a new agent in the catalog.

409.description: An agent with this name already exists

get.summary:
Discover agents that have a skill tagged `tag`. Access-scoped like `list`
(superuser → all; otherwise owner ∪ public ∪ user-grant — see
`agent_access_predicate`). Uses the GIN `idx_agent_skills_tags` via the `@>`
containment operator and `EXISTS` (no join fan-out / DISTINCT).

200.description: Agents with a matching skill tag

409.description: Canonical name or integration identity conflict

post.summary:
Restart an agent's deployment (K8s: scale-to-1; Docker: destroy + recreate).
Owner-or-superuser only.

403.description: Caller does not own this deployment

409.description: Deployment is already running or starting

get.summary:
List the caller's deployments (superuser → all, newest 50 first). Callers
below deployer role get `200 {"available": false}` instead of an error —
see `nasiko_server::unavailable`.

200.description: Deployments, or `{"available": false}` if the caller can't deploy

get.summary:
Server-Sent Events stream of `{"status": ..., "build_id": ...}` on each
status change, polling every 3s until the build reaches `success`/`failed`
(or `{"status": "not_found"}` once, if the build id doesn't exist).
Callers below deployer role get `200 {"available": false}` instead.

200.description: `text/event-stream` of build status updates, or `{"available": false}`

get.summary:
The platform fallback env vars the CP injects into every deployment
(OPENAI_* today). Consumed by `nasiko run` so a local container starts
with the same defaults a CP deployment would get. Deployer-gated: anyone
who can deploy already receives these values inside the containers they deploy.

List agents the caller has uploaded (superuser → all), one row per agent
(most recent upload), joined with live catalog metadata.

post.summary:
Register a new agent from a source zip and queue an asynchronous
build-and-deploy job (poll via `/uploads/{upload_id}` or
`/deploys/{build_id}/stream`). Deployer role required.

400.description: Missing/invalid name, version_tag, or source zip

get.summary:
List the caller's uploads/builds, newest first (superuser → all). Also
mounted at the top-level `/api/upload-status` alias (`status_router`).
Callers below deployer role get `200 {"available": false}` instead of an error.

Get the status of a single upload/build (by `upload_id`, i.e. the build id
as a string). Callers below deployer role, or a non-owner non-superuser,
get `200 {"available": false}` instead of an error.
List an agent's secret names (never decrypted values). Owner-or-superuser only.

post.summary: Create or overwrite one of an agent's secrets. Owner-or-superuser only.

Copy a subset of the caller's own user-scoped secrets into an agent's
secrets_env, re-encrypting them under the agent's key. Owner-or-superuser only.

delete.summary: Delete one of an agent's secrets. Owner-or-superuser only.

404.description: No agent or secret with this name

get.summary: Fetch a single agent by UUID or name, rendered as an A2A AgentCard-shaped envelope.

put.summary: Update an agent's catalog metadata. Owner-or-superuser only.

delete.summary:
Delete an agent and tear down its running containers (best-effort).
Owner-or-superuser only.

get.summary:
Get an agent's current (non-stopped) deployment. Callers who can't deploy
or can't access the agent get `200 {"available": false}` instead of an error.

404.description: No non-stopped deployment for this agent

get.summary:
The agent's **resolved** routing config (attached → owner default →
none), which config is attached, its source, and the inbound format. Owner-or-superuser only.

403.description: Caller is not the agent owner

delete.summary: Detach the config and clear the agent-level pin in one call. Owner-or-superuser only.

403.description: Caller is not the agent owner

patch.summary:
Attach/detach a reusable LLM config to an agent, and optionally change the
inbound SDK format. A config can only be attached if it belongs to the
agent owner. Owner-or-superuser only.

200.description: Updated, with the freshly resolved config

400.description: Config not found/not owned, or unsupported inbound_format

403.description: Caller is not the agent owner

post.summary:
Issue a short-lived agent identity token for a local SDK process. The caller
must own the agent; the signing secret never leaves the control plane.

403.description: Caller is not the agent owner

503.description: LLM router authentication is not configured

post.summary:
Roll back to a previous rollback-eligible version (defaults to the most
recent one) — a synthetic build record so the same SSE polling path works,
no image rebuild. Owner-or-superuser only.

requestBody.description: Optional; omit or send an empty body to use defaults

404.description: No such agent, or no such target version

put.summary:
Rebuild and redeploy an agent from a new source archive, bumping its
version. Runs the build asynchronously (poll via `/uploads/{id}` SSE or
`/deploys/{build_id}/stream`). Owner-or-superuser only.

409.description: Version already exists or is not greater than current

get.summary: List an agent's build/version history.

delete.summary:
Delete a specific version record. Rejects deleting the currently active
version — roll back to another version first. Owner-or-superuser only.

post.summary: Clone a GitHub repo (via the caller's stored OAuth token), then build and deploy it.

502.description: Failed to download the repository archive

post.summary:
Import an agent from an OCI registry: a source-tarball layer is built and
deployed like `/import/upload`; a plain container image is pulled and
deployed directly.

403.description: Registry import disabled or host not allowed

422.description: Registry host not in the allowed list

502.description: Registry unreachable or returned an error

post.summary: Upload a source archive and synchronously build + deploy it as an agent.
post.description:
Meant to be quick and direct, not production-grade robust: unlike its
sibling `/api/agents/upload` (`oss/server/src/agents/upload.rs`), which is
asynchronous, tracked via `upload_status`, and retried on failure through
a real job queue, this runs the whole build-and-deploy pipeline
synchronously inside the request handler, with no progress tracking and
no retry — you get a response once the build either finishes or fails,
and that's it.

400.description: Missing package file or invalid archive

get.summary: List the caller's LLM configs, ordered by name.

200.description: `data` is an array of config objects, each with: id, name, provider, model, fallback_models, temperature, max_tokens, api_key_secret_name, pinned, pinned_model, tier1_model, tier2_model, tier3_model, is_default, created_at, updated_at

post.summary:
Create a named LLM config owned by the caller, optionally storing the
referenced API-key secret and/or marking it as the caller's default.

201.description: `data` is the created config object (id, name, provider, model, fallback_models, temperature, max_tokens, api_key_secret_name, pinned, pinned_model, tier1_model, tier2_model, tier3_model, is_default, created_at, updated_at)

409.description: A config with this name already exists

get.summary: Fetch one of the caller's configs; configs the caller doesn't own read as 404.

200.description: `data` is the config object (id, name, provider, model, fallback_models, temperature, max_tokens, api_key_secret_name, pinned, pinned_model, tier1_model, tier2_model, tier3_model, is_default, created_at, updated_at)

404.description: Unknown id, or not owned by the caller

delete.summary:
Soft-delete one of the caller's configs. Fails while any live agent still
has the config attached.

404.description: Unknown id, or not owned by the caller

409.description: Config is attached to one or more agents

patch.summary:
Partially update one of the caller's configs; absent fields keep their
current value. Use `POST /api/llm-configs/{id}/default` to change the default.

200.description: `data` is the updated config object (id, name, provider, model, fallback_models, temperature, max_tokens, api_key_secret_name, pinned, pinned_model, tier1_model, tier2_model, tier3_model, is_default, created_at, updated_at)

404.description: Unknown id, or not owned by the caller

409.description: Another config with this name already exists

post.summary: Mark one of the caller's configs as their default, clearing any prior default.

200.description: `data` is the config object now marked as default (id, name, provider, model, fallback_models, temperature, max_tokens, api_key_secret_name, pinned, pinned_model, tier1_model, tier2_model, tier3_model, is_default, created_at, updated_at)

404.description: Unknown id, or not owned by the caller

delete.summary:
Clear the default flag on one of the caller's configs, leaving them with no
default. The counterpart to [`set_default`]: without it, once a config was
marked default the flag could only ever move to a *different* config, never
be removed — so "make this not the default" was unreachable, and with a
single config there was no way out at all.
delete.description:
Agents that were falling back to this default resolve to `source: "none"`
afterwards and use the platform key path (see `resolve_agent_config`).

200.description: `data` is the config object, now with `is_default: false`

404.description: Unknown id, or not owned by the caller

get.summary:
List every provider/model with a currently-effective `model_pricing` row,
grouped by provider. Backs the UI provider/model dropdown.

200.description: Currently-effective model catalog, grouped by provider

post.summary:
Agent-facing MCP JSON-RPC gateway. Generic `tools/list` / `tools/call`
JSON-RPC 2.0; request and response bodies are protocol-defined, not
REST-shaped, so they are documented as free-form objects.
post.description:
Authorization rules (docs/MCP_GATEWAY_AGENT_AUTH.md §2.4), all failing
closed:
1. bearer token missing/unknown/revoked → 401
2. `tools/list` (and initialize/ping) → allowed with agent-only identity
3. `tools/call` with no/unknown/dead-flow traceparent → 403
4. `tools/call` where the agent is not a recorded flow participant → 403
5. identity store unreachable → 403

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: `Bearer <MCP_GATEWAY_TOKEN>` — the per-agent gateway credential injected into the container env at deploy time

parameters.name: traceparent
parameters.description: W3C trace context naming the flow this call belongs to — required for `tools/call`; the user identity is resolved from the flow record

202.description: Notification accepted (no `id` in request); empty object body

403.description: `tools/call` outside a live flow the agent participates in, or identity store unavailable

get.summary: `GET /api/mcp/agents/{agent_id}/connectors` — connectors + per-agent status.
get.description:
Same relaxed gate as `list_tool_rules` below (and `set_connector_access`/
`list_connector_tools`, already relaxed by `a9012ded`/`56e46b07`): a caller
who can't manage the whole agent still sees the connector(s) they
themselves can reach (narrowed, not blocked outright) — otherwise this
endpoint (the natural first call before `agent-tools enable`/`set-rule`)
would be the one sibling still hard-denying the exact caller those other
endpoints already permit, making them undiscoverable in practice. This
works with zero relationship to the agent itself, e.g. a connector owner
whose connector was granted to someone else's agent.

If that per-connector filter finds nothing at all (no connector the
caller can manage happens to be attached here), it used to hard-403
unconditionally — but an empty result is also the normal, legitimate
state for a caller who has ordinary access to the agent
([`can_access_agent`] — owner, public, or a plain share) and simply
hasn't attached any connector of their own yet (e.g. they're about to
attach their first one). Only a caller with NEITHER a manageable
connector already here NOR any relationship to the agent at all still
gets the 403.

200.description: Connectors + per-agent status — `data.connectors` is a list

403.description: Caller cannot manage this agent, has no manageable connector already attached, and has no other relationship to it

put.description:
Allows either full agent management, or the connector's own owner acting on
their connector once it's been granted to this agent (see
`ensure_can_manage_agent_connector`) — a connector owner can enable/disable
their own connector on someone else's agent without managing the agent itself.

403.description: Caller cannot manage this connector on this agent

get.summary: `GET /api/mcp/agents/{agent_id}/connectors/{connector_id}/tools` — tools + stances.
get.description:
Same relaxed gate as `set_connector_access`: the connector's own owner can
view its tools/stances on this agent once it's been granted here.

200.description: The connector's tools + effective stances for this agent

403.description: Caller cannot manage this connector on this agent

get.summary: `GET /api/mcp/agents/{agent_id}/tools` — the agent's current tool rules.
get.description:
Agent-wide (every connector's rules at once), so a non-agent-manager never
gets the unfiltered view: if they can't manage the whole agent, the result
is narrowed to only the connector(s) they themselves can manage
(`can_manage_agent_connector` — reachable, and either already granted to
this agent or the caller has at least ordinary access to it), e.g. so
`agent-tools set-rule`'s read-modify-write can find that connector's
existing rules. This works with zero relationship to the agent itself,
e.g. a connector owner whose connector was granted to someone else's agent.

If that filter finds no manageable connector at all, an empty result is
still a normal 200 as long as the caller has at least ordinary access to
the agent ([`can_access_agent`] — owner, public, or a plain share): a
freshly shared agent with no rules configured yet is not a permission
failure. Only a caller with neither a manageable connector already here
nor any relationship to the agent at all gets the 403.

200.description: The agent's tool rules — `data.rules` is a list

403.description: Caller cannot manage this agent, has no manageable connector already attached, and has no other relationship to it

put.description:
Each rule names its own `connector_id`, so the gate is per-connector: full
agent management, or (for each distinct connector referenced) that
connector's own owner acting on a connector already granted to this agent —
same relaxed rule as `set_connector_access`. An empty batch still requires
full agent management, since there's no connector to scope a narrower
check to.

403.description: Caller cannot manage a referenced connector on this agent

`GET /api/mcp/connectors/pinned` — the caller's pinned connectors.

200.description: Recently-used connectors — `data` is a list of connector views

post.summary: `POST /api/mcp/connectors/upload` — multipart zip upload.

400.description: Missing name/zip or upload too large

`POST /api/mcp/connectors/upload-github` — clone a repo instead of a zip.

404.description: No such connector (or not visible to the caller)

delete.summary: `DELETE /api/mcp/connectors/{id}` — delete an owned connector (or any, if admin).

200.description: Connector updated — `data` is the connector view

`GET /api/mcp/connectors/{id}/build-logs` — same ownership check as

200.description: Build container logs — `data` is the log text

200.description: Latest build status for the connector

get.summary: `GET /api/mcp/connectors/{id}/consumers` — agents that have this connector configured.

200.description: Agents that have this connector configured

200.description: Credential status — `data` is `{connector_id, name, connected, auth_type}`

200.description: OAuth status — `data` is `{connector_id, name, authorized, expires_at, scope}`

post.summary: `POST /api/mcp/connectors/{id}/pin` — pin for quick access.

get.summary: `GET /api/mcp/oauth/callback` — public browser redirect target (HTML, not JSON).

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Opaque state minted by the authorize step

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: OAuth error code, if the provider denied

302.description: Redirect back to the requesting app

get.summary: `GET /api/mcp/share-targets?q=` — search users to share a connector with.

`GET /api/mcp/share-targets/resolve?username=` — exact username → user_id,
for `share add`/`share remove` to target someone outside the caller's own
org-visibility scope (unlike `search_targets` above, this is intentionally
NOT scoped — see `service::connectors::resolve_share_target`'s doc comment).
List every configured tier→model mapping, ordered by provider and tier.

put.summary: Upsert one `(provider, tier)` → model mapping. Superuser only.

get.summary: Trace/cost/latency stats for one agent (accepts a UUID or agent name).

parameters.name: start_time
parameters.description:
Optional — the service defaults to the last 24 hours, matching the
other observe endpoints (the UI calls this with no params at all).

get.summary: `GET /api/observe/agents/{agent_ref}/logs`
get.description:
`agent_ref` may be a UUID or an agent name (e.g. `my-agent`).

Returns a merged, time-sorted list of log lines from up to three sources:
  1. Loki (when observability backend is configured)
  2. `proxy_logs` DB table (always)
  3. Container stdout/stderr via the runtime (always)

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Filter by level: INFO | WARN | ERROR | DEBUG

get.summary: `GET /api/observe/agents/{agent_ref}/logs/stream`
get.description:
SSE live-tail stream. `agent_ref` may be a UUID or agent name.

Protocol:
  • Immediately emits the last 30 container log lines as historical context.
  • Then polls every 3 s for new `proxy_logs` rows (since stream opened).
  • Sends an SSE comment `keepalive` every cycle so the connection stays alive.

get.summary: Windowed replica-hours per agent (billing source of truth), optionally bucketed.

parameters.name: start_time
parameters.description: ISO-8601 window start (default: all-time; 30 days ago when `bucket` is set).

parameters.name: agent_id
parameters.description: Optional agent UUID — restricts the report to one agent.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description: Optional series granularity: "hour" | "day". Anything else is ignored.

get.summary: FinOps dashboard: per-agent cost/token rows plus fleet-wide summary.

parameters.name: start_time
parameters.description: ISO-8601 window start (default: 30 days ago). Ignored when `range` is set.

parameters.name: end_time
parameters.description:
ISO-8601 window end (default: now). Without it a past-month selection
means "that month through today" rather than that month.

parameters.name: agent_id
parameters.description: Agent UUID or name — scopes the whole response to one agent.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Exact model id, matched against span model attributes.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description:
Provider name filter (e.g. "openai", "anthropic"), matched against
the `provider` column in `trace_usage` (derived from `model_pricing`).

parameters.name: org_unit
parameters.description:
Org-unit filter — resolved to user_ids by the EE auth layer. OSS
accepts the param but ignores it (no org hierarchy). EE reads it in
the handler and passes user_ids to the service.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description:
"agent" | "workflow" — which attribution source powers the response's
`attributions` field (default "agent").

parameters.name: my_agent
parameters.description:
When `true`, restricts results to agents owned by the caller.
Ignored when `agent_id` is also set (already scoped to one agent).

post.summary: LLM-generated cost insights from the caller-supplied FinOps KPI snapshot.

get.summary: List chat sessions (DB-authoritative, enriched from Tempo when available).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Page size (default 25, max 100). Each row costs one trace-store lookup,
so this bounds the request's real work — it is not just a display limit.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Rows to skip, for offset paging (default 0).

get.summary: Detail for one session: traces, token usage, and cost summary.

404.description: Session not found in the observability backend

get.summary: Detail for one span: attributes, input/output content, and cost.

404.description: Span not found in this trace

get.summary: Detail for one trace: full span tree with per-span token/cost attribution.

post.summary:
Server-side A2A dispatch endpoint. Accepts JSONRPC `message/send` or `message/stream`.
Dispatches to the routing engine (no agent_id), ReAct orchestrator (agent_id=orchestrator),
or a specific agent directly.
post.description:
No gateway required: the server validates the JWT and enforces authorization itself
(see `require_auth`/`Claims`). This handler is the production A2A path.

400.description: Missing/invalid params, or an empty message

403.description: Caller cannot access the targeted agent

404.description: Target agent not found or not running

503.description: No agents available for routing-engine dispatch

post.summary: `POST /api/a2a/upload` — multipart/form-data A2A dispatch entry point.
post.description:
Accepts:
- `query`   (text field, required) — the user's question
- Any number of additional fields treated as file attachments

Each file is base64-encoded and forwarded alongside the query to the orchestrator.

400.description: Missing/invalid multipart, or an empty query field

get.summary:
Aggregated agent-selection stats from the `agent_selection_stats`
materialized view (newest date, most-selected agent first; max 200 rows).

Look up an agent by its UUID or name (registry-entry lookup).
Equivalent to GET /agents/{id} but exposed at the /registries/ path for
clients that use the registry-centric URL scheme.

Returns agents accessible to the current user: owned + public + explicitly granted.
Supports optional `?q` (name/description search), `?status`, `?limit`, `?offset`.
Superusers see all agents.

Agent-only search.  Scoring: GREATEST across (name×2.8, description×2.0, tag score) with tiered
exact/prefix/contains scoring.  Minimum query length: 2 chars.

Search the user directory. The user directory (usernames + emails) is
sensitive (CAT-4), so results are scoped via `AuthService::org_visible_user_ids`
— OSS returns `None` (unrestricted, no org hierarchy to scope by); EE
restricts non-admin callers to their own department/team, same as the MCP
share-target picker (`oss/mcp-gateway`'s `search_share_targets_view`).
An exact username/display-name match bypasses that scope, mirroring
`resolve_share_target`/`departments.rs::resolve`/`teams.rs::resolve` —
a caller who already knows exactly who they're looking for (e.g. a
connector owner sharing outside their own team) can still find them by
typing the full name, they just can't browse/enumerate people outside
their scope via a partial query.
List the caller's secrets (names + metadata only — never decrypted values).

post.summary: Create a secret, or overwrite the value if one with this name already exists.

422.description: Invalid secret name — see `oss/docs` for the naming rule

get.summary: Fetch and decrypt a single secret's value.
Per-agent usage breakdown for the caller, ordered by total tokens.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Case-insensitive substring filter: on the agent name for `by-agent`,
on the model name for `by-model`. Omitted or empty matches everything.

get.summary: Per-provider/model usage breakdown for the caller, ordered by total tokens.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Case-insensitive substring filter: on the agent name for `by-agent`,
on the model name for `by-model`. Omitted or empty matches everything.

get.summary: Per-day usage breakdown for the caller over the last `days` days.

200.description: One row per day with activity

get.summary: Aggregate token usage and cost for the caller over the last `days` days.

List users (superuser-only; EE additionally exposes a role/org-scoped
listing at `/api/org/users` — see `ee/server/src/org_users.rs`).

post.summary:
Create a user. No password is taken — a one-time `access_key`/
`access_secret` pair is minted and returned once; the secret doubles as
the user's login password (see `nasiko-user-creation-contract`).

get.summary: List every admin (`role = 'admin'`) user.

The caller's own user record (superuser-only route; EE overrides this
with the same EE-aware shape as `get_user` — see `ee/server/src/users.rs`).
Agents accessible to the caller — see `accessible_agents_for_user`.
Get a user by id (superuser-only).

put.summary:
Update a user's own-editable fields (superuser-only; EE overrides this
route to additionally accept `department_id`/`team_id` — see
`ee/server/src/users.rs::ee_update_user`). An `is_active: false`
transition here runs the same self-deactivate/last-admin guards as the
dedicated `/deactivate` route.

400.description: Empty username/email or password too short

409.description: Username/email already taken, cannot deactivate the last admin, or user has no local credentials to set a password for

delete.summary:
Delete a user. Rejects self-deletion, deleting the last admin, or a user
who still owns agents (reassign or delete those first).

get.summary:
Agents accessible to a user (owner ∪ public ∪ direct user-grant; EE's
override in `ee/server/src/users.rs` additionally checks team/department
grants).

post.summary:
Deactivate a user and revoke their live tokens. Rejects self-deactivation
and deactivating the last admin.

Mint a fresh `access_key`/`access_secret` pair for a user, replacing any
existing credential, and revoke their live tokens.
Reactivate a previously deactivated user.

put.summary:
Change a user's role and immediately revoke their live tokens. EE wraps
this with a leadership-displacement cascade — see
`ee/server/src/users.rs::ee_change_role`.

A2aJsonRpcRequest.description:
Doc-only stand-in for the real request type (`nasiko_types::a2a::JsonRpcRequest`,
re-exported from the external `a2a-lf` crate, which has no `ToSchema` impl and
can't be given one here). Mirrors its actual JSON-RPC 2.0 shape: `method` is
`"message/send"` or `"message/stream"`; `params` is a `SendMessageRequest` —
see `oss/docs/A2A_PROTOCOL.md` for the full parts/metadata schema.
`metadata.agent_id` selects the dispatch target: absent or `"orchestrator"`
routes through the routing engine/ReAct orchestrator, anything else proxies
directly to that agent (UUID or name).

A2aUploadForm.description:
Multipart form for `POST /api/orchestrator/a2a/upload` — a required `query`
text field, plus any number of additional fields treated as file attachments
(each base64-encoded and forwarded to the orchestrator alongside the query).

AccessibleAgentsResponse.description:
Response envelope for the `accessible-agents` routes — the JSON shape of
`Paginated<AccessibleAgent>` spelled out concretely (see `UserListResponse`).

AdminListResponse.description:
Response envelope for `GET /users/admins` — the JSON shape of
`Paginated<AdminUser>` spelled out concretely (see `UserListResponse`).

transport_path.description:
Path of the agent's advertised JSON-RPC transport (e.g. "/jsonrpc"),
extracted from its AgentCard `supportedInterfaces` at deploy time.
Clients chat via `{base}/api/agents/{id}{transport_path}`.

can_manage.description:
True when the caller may manage this agent (owner or superuser) —
computed with the same predicate the mutating routes enforce
(`crate::acl::can_manage_agent`), so the UI can gate its management
tabs without guessing.

owner_id.description: Owner's user UUID — lets the UI label the owner row in grant lists.

avg_latency_ms.description: p50 trace-level latency for this agent in the window.

cache_creation_tokens.description: Prompt tokens written to provider cache (Anthropic cache creation).

cache_read_tokens.description: Prompt tokens served from provider cache (OpenAI cached / Anthropic cache read).

container_hours.description: Replica-hours this agent consumed in the dashboard window.

is_capped.description:
True when `operations` was capped by the token-aggregation trace
limit — the token/cost fields below undercount the real total.

agents.description: Per-agent breakdown for this bucket (only agents with hours in it).
Sessions-derived rows — includes agents that have since been deleted.

buckets.description: Time series, present only when the `bucket` query param is set.

total_hours.description: Replica-hours across all listed agents within the window.

live_replicas.description: Replicas live right now among the sessions that overlapped this window.

AgentSearchResponse.description:
Agent search envelope — mirrors Python's `{agents, total, max_score}` and the
existing `UserSearchResponse` shape so both search surfaces are consistent.

AgentSearchResult.description:
One agent search hit: all agent fields plus its computed relevance `score`.
`_total` is the pre-limit match count (window function) — carried per row and
hoisted into the response envelope, not serialized on each item.

AgentSummary.description: Lightweight projection returned by the by-skill discovery endpoint.

AgentUsagePage.description:
Doc-only schema for `crate::Paginated<AgentUsage>` (the generic envelope
itself is not utoipa-annotated).

AttachLlmConfigRequest.description:
Attach/detach a reusable LLM config to an agent, and optionally change the inbound format.
A config can only be attached if it belongs to the agent owner (per-user ownership keeps the
referenced secret in the owner's store). Owner-only (or superuser).

inbound_format.description: Optionally change which SDK the agent's code speaks (drives deploy injection).

llm_config_id.description:
Double-option distinguishes the three cases: absent ⇒ leave unchanged; `null` ⇒ detach
(fall back to the owner's default); a UUID ⇒ attach that config.

pinned_model.description:
Agent-level model pin. Overrides the config's `pinned_model`. Double-option:
absent ⇒ leave unchanged; `null` ⇒ clear pin; string ⇒ set pin.

api_key_secret_name.description:
Name of the caller's `user_secrets` row holding the provider API key. None ⇒ the
platform-key path.

is_default.description: Mark this as the caller's default (clears any prior default).

tier1_model.description:
Per-config tier→model overrides. When set, the smart router uses these instead of
the global `model_registry` for this config's provider.

is_superuser.description:
Separate from `role` — `role` is a `user_role` enum value
(admin/department_manager/team_lead/team_member/member), never
"superuser". This is the one flag that actually grants unrestricted
access (bypasses org-visibility scoping, gates superuser-only routes
like MCP toolkit registration) — see CLAUDE.md's `role` vs
`is_superuser` note.

CreateUserResponse.description:
One-time credential material — the only time `access_secret` is ever
returned; the server stores only its hash from here on.

EmptyEnvelope.description:
Doc-only schema for the standard `ApiResponse` envelope when a handler has
no payload to return (`ApiResponse::ok(json!(null), …)`): `data` is always
JSON null, so only `status_code` and `message` carry information.

spend_by_agent.description:
Pre-computed spend split for the selected window: top-5 agents by spend
plus an "Others" catchall, ready to feed a pie/donut chart without any
client-side aggregation.

avg_latency_ms.description: Fleet-wide p50 latency (label kept for UI backward compat).

estimated_cost.description: Sum of rows explicitly priced using inferred rates or usage evidence.

total_container_hours.description:
Replica-hours consumed in the dashboard window — includes agents that
have since been deleted (their sessions survive deletion).

unknown_confidence_calls.description: Older materializations without recorded pricing confidence.

unpriced_calls.description:
Calls in the window that consumed tokens but carry no cost (no price row
for the model — e.g. a custom provider with no price book). `SUM(cost_usd)`
silently skips these, so `total_cost` under-reports; this surfaces the gap
as a known number rather than a smaller one.

cache_creation_tokens.description: Prompt tokens written to provider cache (Anthropic cache creation).

cache_read_tokens.description: Prompt tokens served from provider cache (OpenAI cached / Anthropic cache read).

repository.description: `"owner/repo"` — the caller's GitHub connection must already be authorized for it.

ImportUploadForm.description:
Multipart form for `POST /api/import/upload` — a single `package` file
field holding a zip/tar.gz with `AgentCard.json` + `Dockerfile` at its root.

JsonRpcErrorBody.description: Doc-only stand-in for the JSON-RPC error envelope `A2aDispatchError` renders.

change_pct.description:
`(current - previous) / previous * 100`, rounded to 2dp. `None` when
`previous == 0` — an undefined percentage, not a fabricated 0 or ∞.

LlmConfigResponse.description:
Response envelope for `GET /{id}/llm-config` — documents the shape of the
ad hoc `serde_json::json!` object the handler returns.

llm_config.description: The resolved config the router will actually use, or `null`.

llm_config_id.description: Which config is attached; `null` ⇒ owner default / none.

pinned_model.description: Agent-level model pin, overriding the config's own `pinned_model`, or `null`.

LlmConfigUpdateResponse.description:
Response envelope for `PATCH /{id}/llm-config` — documents the shape of
the ad hoc `serde_json::json!` object the handler returns.

pinned_model.description: Agent-level model pin after applying this update, or `null`.

LogLine.description: A single log line returned to the client.

level.description: "INFO" | "WARN" | "ERROR" | "DEBUG" — may be None for raw container output

trace_id.description: Present when the log was emitted in the context of an A2A flow

McpEnvelope.description:
Doc-only schema for the standard MCP `ApiResponse` envelope
(`{"data": …, "status_code": N, "message": "…"}`). Most `/api/mcp/*`
payloads are service-layer `serde_json::Value` views, so `data` is
documented as a free-form object; each route's response description says
what it carries.

ModelEntry.description:
One model within a provider group. Field names mirror the `model_pricing` columns;
prices are null when the model has no currently-effective price row.

pricing_available.description:
Whether a currently-effective price row backs this model. `false` ⇒ the model is
served but its cost is not tracked (shown as "cost not tracked" in the UI, not $0).

ModelMappingListEnvelope.description: `crate::mcp::ApiResponse` envelope around a list of [`ModelMapping`] rows.

ModelUsagePage.description:
Doc-only schema for `crate::Paginated<ModelUsage>` (the generic envelope
itself is not utoipa-annotated).

ProviderCatalog.description: A provider and its models, e.g. `{ "provider": "openai", "models": [...] }`.

display_name.description: Human-friendly name of the custom provider, if this is a DB-registered custom endpoint.

provider_id.description: UUID of the custom provider, if this is a DB-registered custom endpoint.

ProviderCatalogEnvelope.description: `crate::mcp::ApiResponse` envelope around a list of [`ProviderCatalog`] groups.

RegenerateCredentialsResponse.description:
One-time credential material — the only time `access_secret` is ever
returned; the server stores only its hash from here on.

reference.description:
OCI reference: `"registry.host/owner/name[:tag]"`. The host must be
allowed: a built-in default, the settings-page registry URL, or
`REGISTRY_IMPORT_ALLOWED_HOSTS`.

RestartDeploymentResponse.description:
Response envelope for `restart_deployment` — documents the shape of the ad
hoc `serde_json::json!` object the handler returns. `deployment_id` is
omitted if the runtime restart succeeded but bookkeeping failed;
`warnings` is omitted entirely when empty.

input_tokens.description:
Per-turn token split. `cumulative_token_count_total` is `input+output`;
the cache counts are tracked separately and are not folded into it.

RouterStatsRow.description:
One row of `RouterStatsResponse` — mirrors the ad hoc `serde_json::json!`
object the handler builds per row (numeric averages are stringified to
preserve `rust_decimal` precision through JSON).

cache_read_tokens.description: Prompt tokens served from / written to provider cache, over the session.

latency_avg.description: Mean trace duration, which is what the KPI strip labels "Avg latency".

latency_p99.description:
The session page renders this KPI (`s.latency_p99`); it was silently
`0.0 s` for every session while the field didn't exist in the response.

title.description:
LLM-derived session name from `chat_sessions`. `None` for sessions that
never went through chat (CLI / direct A2A), where the id is the heading.

cost_summary.description:
Carries the prompt/completion split the Usage tab renders; the service
already computed it and used to sum it away before serializing.

provider.description:
GenAI provider and model, promoted out of the nested `attributes` blob
so the detail pane reads one field instead of walking a semconv tree.

operation.description:
The greyed second label on a span row (`chat`, `git.clone`, …).
`None` when no attribute names one — the UI must not synthesise it
from the span name.

provider.description: GenAI provider (`openai`, `anthropic`, …), for the row's glyph.

slices.description:
Top-5 agents by spend, followed by an "Others" entry when there are
more than 5 agents. Empty when there is no spend in the window.

pct.description: Percentage of total window spend, rounded to 2dp.

activate_version.description:
`true` (the default) for a real deploy — the new version becomes
active, archiving whatever was running before. `nasiko push` sets
this `false`: it only makes an image available in the registry
without deploying it, so it must not claim the new version is now
active or archive the version that's genuinely still running.

UpdateAgentForm.description:
Multipart form for `PUT /{id}/update` — a `.zip` `source` file plus optional
`version` (a strategy keyword `auto`/`patch`/`minor`/`major`, or an explicit
semver string greater than the current version) and `changelog` fields.

UpdateLlmConfigRequest.description:
Partial update — every field is optional. Absent fields keep their current value.
`is_default` is not touched here — use `POST /llm-configs/{id}/default`.

role.description: Basic role update without cascade (use /role for leadership promotions).

UploadAndDeployForm.description:
Multipart form for `POST /agents/upload` — a `.zip` `source`/`file` field
(an `AgentCard.json` + `Dockerfile` package) plus agent metadata fields.

env.description: JSON object of extra env vars, e.g. `{"FOO":"bar"}`.

inbound_format.description: `openai` (default) | `anthropic` | `gemini` — which SDK the agent's code speaks.

writable.description:
`"true"`/`"false"` to mount / not mount a persistent, private-per-agent
directory at `/workspace`. Tri-state: omit the field to keep an existing
agent's stored setting (false for a new agent) — the CLI only sends it
when `--writable` was passed.

writable_path.description:
Container-side mount target for the writable volume (`--writable-path`).
Absolute path; implies `writable`. Omit to keep an existing agent's
stored path (`/workspace` for a new agent).

UploadStatusListResponse.description:
Response envelope for `GET /upload-status` — documents the shape of the ad
hoc `serde_json::json!` object the handler returns.

UploadZipForm.description: Doc-only schema for the multipart form consumed by `upload_zip`.

env.description: JSON object of env vars for the built server, as a string field.

source.description: Zip archive with the MCP server source (also accepted as `file`).

UserListResponse.description:
Response envelope for `GET /users` — the JSON shape of `Paginated<UserRow>`,
spelled out concretely since `Paginated<T>`'s generic isn't monomorphized
for `ToSchema` here.

UserSearchResponse.description:
Response envelope for `/search/users` — documents the shape of the ad hoc
`serde_json::json!` object the handler returns.

UserSearchResult.description:
User search. Field boosts: username×3.0, display_name×2.5, email×1.5.
Scoring: exact (100×boost) > prefix (90×boost) > contains (70×boost).
Minimum query length: 2 chars. Sort: score DESC, username ASC.
Returns all matching users (no limit).

cache_creation_tokens.description: Prompt tokens written to provider cache (Anthropic cache creation).

cache_read_tokens.description: Prompt tokens served from provider cache (OpenAI cached / Anthropic cache read).
